questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

The diagram shows the costs and benefits of producing a good. The good has negative externalities in production and positive externalities in consumption. The free market equilibrium is at point X. What is the new equilibrium point when the externalities are taken into consideration? costs, MSC benefits B $ MPC A X MSC C D MSB MPB MSB O output

The Airports Commission in the UK recommended an expansion of airport X rather than airport Y. In considering the social costs and benefits of this decision, what would be taken into account when calculating the external cost?

options.A: the additional noise pollution suffered by residents local to airport X
options.B: the financial loss suffered by airlines operating at airport Y
options.C: the increase in profits of the firm operating airport X
options.D: the monetary cost of the construction to expand airport X

questions.questionText: What is a correct statement of the equi-marginal utility rule?

options.A: The marginal utility of X must equal the marginal utility of Y.
options.B: The marginal utility of X divided by the price of X must equal the marginal utility of Y divided by the price of Y.
options.C: The marginal utility of X divided by the price of Y must equal the marginal utility of Y divided by the price of Y.
options.D: The price of X must equal the price of Y.

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct?

options.A: A budget line shows the combinations of two goods which can be bought with a given income.
options.B: A budget line shows the combinations of two goods which a consumer wants to buy.
options.C: A budget line shows the difference between income and expenditure.
options.D: A budget line shows the maximum potential output of two goods with given resources.

questions.questionText: In the diagram, YL and YM show two budget lines for a consumer of a product, X, when its price changes. IC and IC are two indifference curves, representing the consumer’s preferences

The list provides characteristics of the market in which firm X operates. ● Firms in the market spend a lot of money on advertising. ● Firms in the market experience a high level of uncertainty. ● Start-up costs for new firms entering the market are relatively high. ● The largest five firms in the market control 85% of total sales. In which market structure is firm X operating?

options.A: monopoly
options.B: monopolistic competition
options.C: oligopoly
options.D: perfect competition

questions.questionText: What explains why, in long-run equilibrium in monopolistic competition, firms make only normal profits?

options.A: consumer resistance
options.B: decreasing returns to scale
options.C: differentiated products
options.D: freedom of entry and exit

questions.questionText: The diagram shows four possible output levels of a firm. At its current level of output, the firm’s product has a price elasticity of demand of exactly –1. Which output is the firm selling? MC cost, revenue AC

options.B: C AR O A D MR quantity

questions.questionText: Which conditions enable price discrimination?
The diagram shows a firm producing at Q on short-run average cost SRAC .
Which change would make it easier for a cartel to operate effectively?

options.A: an increase in competition from closely related industries
options.B: an increase in the number of firms in the industry
options.C: an increase in the range of products made by cartel members
options.D: an increase in the stability of the market for its products

questions.questionText: Some workers in a low-paid job decide to work longer hours to increase their disposable income. However, this decision reduces state-provided benefits, leaving them worse off. What does this describe?

options.A: debt trap
options.B: liquidity trap
options.C: poverty trap
options.D: unemployment trap

questions.questionText: What indicates that nationalisation has taken place?

options.A: a firm buys supplies locally rather than from international sources
options.B: a firm moves from private ownership to state ownership
options.C: a firm restricts ownership of its shares to citizens of its own country
options.D: a firm switches sales to the domestic market from the international market

questions.questionText: Too many flights in the airline industry cause unnecessary damage to the environment. Which measure is most likely to result in the socially optimal number of flights?

options.A: a complete ban on flights removing all private and external costs
options.B: greater deregulation of the global airline industry
options.C: publishing information to highlight the negative effects of flying on the environment
options.D: the payment of a subsidy per passenger equal to the difference between the private and social benefit

questions.questionText: A government is worried about the increasing monopsony power of employers in the wage bargaining process. Which policy combination is most likely to improve the wages and employment prospects of workers? trade union immigration national powers controls minimum wage

options.A: strengthen relax cut
options.B: strengthen strengthen raise
options.C: weaken relax cut
options.D: weaken strengthen raise

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the labour market for fruit pickers in country X. wage marginal wage W average wage average revenue product marginal revenue product O quantity of labourers If the market was originally in equilibrium, what would happen to wages and employment if a minimum wage of W were imposed? wages employment

options.A: fall fall
options.B: fall rise
options.C: rise fall
options.D: rise rise

questions.questionText: What would not be regarded as an example of a possible negative impact of rapid economic growth?

options.A: Greater production could result in greater atmospheric pollution.
options.B: A higher level of income could cause a higher balance of trade deficit.
options.C: Increased AD could cause domestic inflation to increase.
options.D: Increased GDP could generate greater tax receipts.

questions.questionText: How can GDP at market prices be calculated if GDP at factor cost is known?

options.A: add taxes, add subsidies
options.B: add taxes, subtract subsidies
options.C: subtract taxes, add subsidies
options.D: subtract taxes, subtract subsidies

questions.questionText: Which combination indicates that GDP per capita is likely to be an accurate indicator of living standards in a country over time? hidden economy quality of goods and income distribution as % of GDP services produced

options.A: equal large constant
options.B: unequal large improving
options.C: equal small improving
options.D: unequal small constant

questions.questionText: Which statement about unemployment is correct?

options.A: Cyclical unemployment is caused by the occupational immobility of labour.
options.B: Frictional unemployment is caused by a lack of information on jobs in the labour market.
options.C: Structural unemployment is caused by a deficiency in aggregate demand.
options.D: Voluntary unemployment is caused by variations in the demand for labour in the year.

questions.questionText: The graph shows the percentage unemployed in a country for the period 2017–2021. 8.5 % 8 7.5 6.5 5.5 4.5 2017 2018 2019 2020 2021 What is the most likely cause of the change in unemployment?

options.A: a reduction in government expenditure
options.B: a reduction in interest rates
options.C: a reduction in investment by firms
options.D: a slowdown in growth in the global economy

questions.questionText: What is the definition of liquidity?

options.A: the ability of the foreign exchange market to buy foreign currency
options.B: the support a central bank provides for commercial banks
options.C: the ease with which an asset can be converted into cash
options.D: the reaction of governments to a global financial crisis

questions.questionText: What will decrease if an open economy experiences a positive output gap?

options.A: general price level
options.B: import spending
options.C: spare capacity
options.D: wage rates

questions.questionText: Which statement does not correctly characterise the Monetarist view of the way in which the economy operates?

options.A: Inflation is always caused by increases in the money supply in the long run.
options.B: The long-run aggregate supply curve is vertical in shape.
options.C: The velocity of circulation of money is highly unstable.
options.D: Wages are flexible both upwards and downwards.

questions.questionText: In an economy, the marginal propensity to consume is 0.2, the marginal propensity to save is 0.3, the marginal propensity to tax is 0.3 and the marginal propensity to import is 0.2 at all levels of income. What would be the most likely consequence of an increase in government expenditure of $1000m?

options.A: Import expenditure would increase by $200m.
options.B: Import expenditure would increase by $1000m.
options.C: Tax revenues would increase by $75m.
options.D: Tax revenues would increase by $375m.

questions.questionText: A developing (low-income) economy is heavily dependent on the production of primary products.

options.A: The company introduces new technology to the economy.
options.B: The company provides diversification of production for the economy.
options.C: The company provides skills training for local workers.
options.D: The company purchases non-renewable local construction materials for the factory.

questions.questionText: An economy adopts an expansionary monetary policy to boost employment. A result of this policy is that the consumer price index rises at an accelerating rate. Which curve could represent this?

options.A: Kuznets curve
options.B: Laffer curve
options.C: Lorenz curve
options.D: Phillips curve

questions.questionText: A government wishes to increase economic efficiency in the country. It raises the rate of income tax which leads to the emigration of high-earning skilled workers that the country needs. How would this outcome be described? government negative market failure failure externality

options.A: no no yes
options.B: no yes no
options.C: yes yes no
options.D: yes no no

questions.questionText: An economy is operating at full employment. Which policy is most likely to lead to an increase in real national output without an increase in the rate of inflation in the short term?

options.A: additional spending on subsidies to increase export earnings
options.B: the central bank introduces quantitative easing
options.C: labour market reforms result in increased output per hour worked
